about:

The firm supplies a broad range of electronic parts including connectors, relays, switches, power supplies, displays, enclosures, and automation control components. In addition to distribution, it offers sheet metal fabrication and off‑shore PCB supply chain services with quick‑turnaround production. Waterbury Electronic Supply emphasizes a “Distribution With a Personal Touch” approach, guided by principles of fair pricing, responsive service, and helping customers reduce costs. The company states it will direct customers to alternative providers when it cannot meet a need.

Watson Metals Co. operates from State Road, North Carolina, in Surry County. The company traces its roots to 1988, when it began as a locally owned and operated shop serving friends and neighbors in the surrounding area. No founder names are disclosed in public materials.

The shop provides metal fabrication and welding services, including sheet metal work, custom metal projects, and on-site welding. It also rents cranes, boom trucks, hoists, and other heavy equipment. The facility sits just off Highway 77, with enough floor space for custom fabrication and on-site sheet metal storage. Headcount, annual volume, and part-number counts are not published.

Customers range from homeowners needing benches, ladders, or custom railings to commercial contractors requiring rebar cages for elevator shafts and construction firms moving heavy loads. The company serves both residential and commercial clients across Surry County, Wilkes County, and the broader Foothills region.

Watson Metals emphasizes its local ownership, personalized service, and willingness to accept walk-in customers without prepared blueprints. On-site welding and a full crane-rental fleet are highlighted as key differentiators, backed by three decades in business.

name: Wayne Wire
old_description: Since 1943, Wayne Wire Cloth Products has been the trusted supplier of high-quality filtration components to Fortune 500 companies worldwide.
about:
Wayne Wire Cloth Products was founded in 1943 in Wayne, Michigan, and established its headquarters in Kalkaska, Michigan, in 1950. The company has operated under its current ownership since a 1996 purchase and expanded internationally with a manufacturing operation in Juárez, Mexico, formed in 2005 and later organized as Wayne Wire International in 2024.

The company produces precision wire cloth and filtration components using processes that include expanded foil mesh production, shearing, rolling, convoluting, manual and automated pressing, welding (TIG, MIG, resistance), soldering, silver and nickel/gold brazing in vacuum furnaces, ultrasonic and chemical cleaning, inspection, laser marking, custom tooling, precision machining, and rapid prototyping. Manufacturing occurs at facilities in Kalkaska and Hillman, Michigan, and Juárez, Mexico.

Wayne Wire serves aerospace (with NADCAP and AS9100D certification), automotive and transportation (supplying high-volume components to manufacturers and Tier 1 suppliers), medical devices, refrigeration and HVAC, municipal and industrial water systems, and supplemental restraint systems such as air bag components. Its customers include Fortune 500 companies worldwide.

The company emphasizes a commitment to quality, service, and innovation, highlighting zero-defect manufacturing for safety-critical applications and more than 80 years of manufacturing excellence in filtration.

name: Wei Chuan USA
old_description: For over five decades, Wei-Chuan USA's passion for delicious food has allowed our customers to enjoy authentic Chinese flavors: every recipe balances tradition with innovation to make meals that everyone can enjoy.
about:
Wei Chuan USA was founded in 1972 in Los Angeles by brothers Thomas and Robert Huang, recent immigrants from Taiwan who missed the authentic flavors of home. The company opened its first plant in Los Angeles in 1975 and expanded with a second facility in Tennessee in 2006. In 2018, the corporate headquarters moved to City of Industry, California, while the Tennessee plant remains a key production site.

The company manufactures a wide range of Chinese food products including gyoza, potstickers, spring rolls, egg rolls, buns, dumplings, wontons, wrappers, entrées, shumai, and a natural, organic, and vegetarian line. Production takes place in two USDA Grant of Inspection establishments that are also FDA-approved, operating under certified HACCP, GMP, and SSOP programs. An in-house R&D team of food scientists, nutritionists, and chefs develops and tests new recipes, balancing traditional flavors with modern convenience.

Wei Chuan USA serves both retail grocery channels and food‑service operators across the United States. Its products are distributed through a network of branch offices in California, Texas, New Jersey, Illinois, and Georgia, reaching supermarkets, Asian specialty stores, and restaurant distributors. The company also supplies a dedicated food‑service category for bulk and institutional use.

The founders started the business because they believed food is a cultural bridge that connects people to their roots. The company’s stated mission is to be the provider of high‑quality Chinese food products in the U.S., upholding tradition while embracing innovation to make authentic flavors convenient for everyone.

about:
Welding Shop & MFG, LLC operates from Cheyenne, Wyoming, where it began in 1975 as The Welding Shop under founders Gerald (Jerry) and JoAnn Pauli. The business remains family-owned and is now run by their sons, Gary and Dwayne Pauli. In 2011 the company adopted its current name, Welding Shop & MFG, LLC, while continuing to serve the surrounding region from its location at 508 East 1st Street.

The shop provides welding, custom fabrication, and machine work, including aluminum welding, drive-shaft repair, ornamental metalwork, handrails, and safety window guards. Since 2000 it has manufactured its own line of Paulibuilt trailers — ranging from utility and sports models to commercial haulers — and offers a full trailer parts department opened in 2012. Mobile welding services are available, and the facility stocks a large inventory of iron, steel, and aluminum for both production and customer projects.

Customers include local contractors, agricultural operators, transportation firms, and recreational trailer owners. The company has performed work for the railroad industry, as noted in customer feedback, and serves both commercial and private clients needing trailer repair, preventive maintenance, hydraulic fitting repair, and custom-built trailers.

The Pauli family emphasizes customer service, honesty, integrity, and reliability as core values, with a motto of “FOR ALL YOUR WELDING & TRAILER NEEDS.” The focus on building long-lasting trailers and offering fast, friendly service is presented as the foundation of their reputation.

about:
Wesco Electrical Supply was founded in 1922 in Bangor, Maine, as an electrical products and solutions provider. The company has grown into a global distributor of electrical, communications, and utility products, with corporate headquarters now in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

Wesco operates as a distributor and supply chain services provider, offering more than 1.5 million products across categories including electrical and lighting, communications and networking, power generation and distribution, and security. The company provides project coordination, forecasting, grid hardening services, program management, hardware inspection, and ground assembly rotation. With approximately 20,000 employees serving 150,000 customers in over 50 countries, Wesco manages a vast distribution network.

The company serves industries such as communications and networking, power generation and distribution, electrical and lighting, security, battery energy storage systems, and AI inference at the edge. Its customers include utilities, contractors, industrial facilities, and commercial builders seeking electrical infrastructure solutions.

Wesco emphasizes a high-performance continuous improvement culture and positions itself as a world leader in electrical, communications, and utility distribution.

about:
West Florida Components was founded in 2005 in Tarpon Springs, Florida, as an online supplier of electronic components and parts. The business is now part of Supply Shield, which operates a warehouse in St. Petersburg, Florida, though the facility is not open to the public.

The company stocks a broad range of electronic components including semiconductors, capacitors, diodes, transistors, resistors, rubber feet, project boxes, and many other categories. It emphasizes that all advertised parts are physically in its warehouse and ready to ship, with most orders shipping the same day if payment is received by 1:00 PM. The catalog also includes obsolete and hard-to-find items, and the company invites customers to call for assistance locating specific parts.

West Florida Components serves customers working on electronics projects, from hobbyists to professionals needing replacement or legacy components. Its specialization in obsolete parts makes it a resource for maintenance and repair operations where discontinued components are required.

The company differentiates itself by guaranteeing that listed parts are in stock, offering same-day shipping on paid orders, and providing toll-free customer support to help buyers identify the right components.

name: West Hartford Solar
old_description: West Hartford Solar was founded by Dan Hovey with one simple mission: to make solar accessible, personal and ethical. What started as a solo journey has grown into a regional team serving customers throughout New England.
about:
West Hartford Solar is based in West Hartford, Connecticut. The company was founded by Dan Hovey with a mission to make solar energy accessible, personal, and ethical. What began as a solo endeavor has grown into a regional team serving customers across New England.

The firm operates as a licensed solar installer covering Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New York. It manages projects in-house from design and permitting through installation and system activation. Installation crews work directly in Connecticut, while partnerships with Earthlight Technologies and New York State Solar Farm extend coverage into Massachusetts and New York. A team of senior consultants supports clients across western Massachusetts, the Connecticut River Valley, southeastern Connecticut, and the Northwest Hills.

Customers include homeowners, businesses, schools, nonprofits, and municipalities. The company has worked with corporate facilities, housing authorities, and local government projects to build custom solar solutions that lower operating costs and meet sustainability goals.

West Hartford Solar emphasizes transparent pricing with access to multiple financing options and no hidden markups. Each client receives a dedicated local representative backed by a regional support team, guiding them from initial consultation through post-installation questions. The founder’s original goal — making solar stress-free and ethical — continues to shape the company’s approach.

name: West Tennessee Solar Exhibit
old_description: More than 25 acres contain a solar array of approximately 21,000 fixed-tilt, ground-mounted photovoltaic solar panels. Electricity generated is distributed through purchase agreements with local utility Chickasaw Electric Cooperative and Tennessee Valley Authority.
about:
The West Tennessee Solar Exhibit is located in Stanton, Tennessee. The project originated from a $62.5-million allocation of federal American Recovery and Reinvestment Act funds to the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development in 2009. The department contracted with the University of Tennessee to oversee the creation and operation of the solar farm through the UT Research Foundation. Signal Energy, LLC of Chattanooga designed and built the array in 2011, with grid connection achieved in early 2012.

The facility spans more than 25 acres and houses approximately 21,000 fixed-tilt, ground-mounted photovoltaic panels. Electricity generated is sold under purchase agreements with Chickasaw Electric Cooperative and the Tennessee Valley Authority. In addition to power production, the site hosts SPECTRUM, an educational exhibit that walks visitors through the history, current technology, and future of solar energy in Tennessee through interactive displays and games.

The operation serves the advanced energy and renewable energy sectors, with direct utility customers including Chickasaw Electric Cooperative and TVA. The exhibit targets homeowners, business owners, students, and educators, offering ideas for residential solar installations, science-fair projects, and career pathways. Partners in the effort include Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council, the Tennessee Renewable Energy & Economic Development Council, and multiple state agencies.

The initiative was launched under the Volunteer State Solar Initiative, a comprehensive program focused on job creation, education, renewable power production, and technology commercialization. The exhibit aims to connect visitors with practical solar applications and inspire the next generation of energy professionals.
